evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Gen: Joseph declares himself unprompted, ʾănî yôsēp hăʿôd ʾābî ḥāy, and the brothers are struck dumb, nibhălû mippānāyw. Q: Joseph asks a leading question, hal ʿalimtum mā faʿaltum bi-Yūsufa wa-akhīh, and they guess, a-innaka la-anta Yūsuf? Then: ana Yūsufu wa-hādhā akhī qad manna llāhu ʿalaynā. Who caused the crime. Gen: God did it, lōʾ-ʾattem šəlaḥtem ʾōtî hēnnâ kî hāʾĕlōhîm, ləmiḥyâ šəlāḥanî ʾĕlōhîm. Q: Satan did it, min baʿdi an nazagha sh-shayṭānu baynī wa-bayna ikhwatī, and God's role is gentle steering, inna rabbī laṭīfun limā yashāʾ. Gen: no confession and no word of forgiveness here, only wəʿattâ ʾal-tēʿāṣəbû and kisses and tears. Q: the brothers confess, wa-in kunnā la-khāṭiʾīn, and Joseph pardons them at once, lā tathrība ʿalaykumu l-yawma yaghfiru llāhu lakum. Gen postpones the request for forgiveness to Gen 50:17. The token changes. Gen: Jacob disbelieves (wayyāpog libbô kî lōʾ-heʾĕmîn lāhem) until he sees the ʿăgālôt, wattəḥî rûaḥ yaʿăqōb. Q: Jacob already knows (innī la-ajidu rīḥa Yūsuf), and the shirt thrown on his face restores his sight, fa-rtadda baṣīran ... a-lam aqul lakum innī aʿlamu mina llāhi mā lā taʿlamūn.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero reveals his identity to his brothers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Father revives on hearing the hero lives [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero declares that God turned the brothers' deed to good [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero forgives his brothers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Father revives on hearing the hero lives (weight 6.0); Hero reveals his identity to his brothers (weight 6.0); Hero declares that God turned the brothers' deed to good (weight 5.6); Hero forgives his brothers (weight 5.6). Pair score 49.5.

Only in Joseph makes himself known; the wagons sent for Jacob: Hero warns his brothers not to quarrel on the journey home; Hero gives his brothers changes of clothing, with a larger gift to the favorite; Hero made 'father' (chief adviser) to the king; Wagons sent from Egypt to carry the father and families; Hero weeps so loudly that the Egyptians and the king's house hear; Brothers or father and son fall on each other's necks and weep; The family is settled apart in the land of Goshen.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 101 more.

passages.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ

passages.text: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

passages.note: Which of Noah's household enter the ark and survive [divergence between the texts] (The household on board: Gen has all of Noah's family, by name, eight persons (bāʾ nōaḥ wᵉšēm wᵉḥām wāyepet bᵉnê-nōaḥ wᵉʾēšet nōaḥ ûšᵉlōšet nᵉšê-bānāyw); Q has his family 'except the one against whom the word went before' plus the few believers (wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu wa-man āmana wa-mā āmana maʿahu illā qalīl). One son refuses, is called in vain (yā bunayya rkab maʿanā) and drowns (fa-kāna mina l-mughraqīn).)
passages.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וּבָאתָ֙ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֔ה אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֛יךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֥ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ

passages.text: בְּעֶ֨צֶם הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ בָּ֣א נֹ֔חַ וְשֵׁם וְחָ֥ם וָיֶ֖פֶת בְּנֵי נֹ֑חַ וְאֵ֣שֶׁת נֹ֗חַ וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת נְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתָּ֖ם אֶל הַתֵּבָֽה

passages.text: وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

passages.note: How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts] (Earth and sky are both stopped: yā arḍu blaʿī māʾaki wa-yā samāʾu aqliʿī wa-ghīḍa l-māʾu vs wayyissākᵉrû maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm waʾărubbōt haššāmayim wayyikkālēʾ haggešem ... wayyaʿăbēr ʾĕlōhîm rûaḥ ... wayyāšōkkû hammāyim. Changed: God commands the earth and the sky directly by word in Q; in Gen he sends a wind and the waters recede slowly over 150 days.)
passages.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת כָּל הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֨וּחַ֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם

passages.note: How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts] (Earth and sky are both stopped: yā arḍu blaʿī māʾaki wa-yā samāʾu aqliʿī wa-ghīḍa l-māʾu vs wayyissākᵉrû maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm waʾărubbōt haššāmayim wayyikkālēʾ haggešem ... wayyaʿăbēr ʾĕlōhîm rûaḥ ... wayyāšōkkû hammāyim. passages.text: וַיִּסָּֽכְרוּ֙ מַעְיְנֹ֣ת תְּה֔וֹם וַֽאֲרֻבֹּ֖ת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיִּכָּלֵ֥א הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם מִן הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

passages.note: How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts] (Earth and sky are both stopped: yā arḍu blaʿī māʾaki wa-yā samāʾu aqliʿī wa-ghīḍa l-māʾu vs wayyissākᵉrû maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm waʾărubbōt haššāmayim wayyikkālēʾ haggešem ... wayyaʿăbēr ʾĕlōhîm rûaḥ ... wayyāšōkkû hammāyim. Changed: God commands the earth and the sky directly by word in Q; in Gen he sends a wind and the waters recede slowly over 150 days.)
passages.text: وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ وَقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِىِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

passages.note: Noah's standing before God: blameless, or in need of forgiveness [divergence between the texts] (Noah's standing: Gen calls him nōaḥ ʾîš ṣaddîq tāmîm ... ʾet-hāʾĕlōhîm hithallek-nōaḥ; in Q he is warned not to be among the ignorant (innī aʿiẓuka an takūna mina l-jāhilīn) and pleads wa-illā taghfir lī wa-tarḥamnī akun mina l-khāsirīn.)
passages.text: אֵ֚לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת נֹ֔חַ נֹ֗חַ אִ֥ישׁ צַדִּ֛יק תָּמִ֥ים הָיָ֖ה בְּדֹֽרֹתָ֑יו אֶת הָֽאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽתְהַלֶּךְ נֹֽחַ

passages.note: Noah's standing before God: blameless, or in need of forgiveness [divergence between the texts] (Noah's standing: Gen calls him nōaḥ ʾîš ṣaddîq tāmîm ... ʾet-hāʾĕlōhîm hithallek-nōaḥ; in Q he is warned not to be among the ignorant (innī aʿiẓuka an takūna mina l-jāhilīn) and pleads wa-illā taghfir lī wa-tarḥamnī akun mina l-khāsirīn.)
passages.text: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَٰلِحٍ فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ إِنِّىٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ

passages.note: Noah's standing before God: blameless, or in need of forgiveness [divergence between the texts] (Noah's standing: Gen calls him nōaḥ ʾîš ṣaddîq tāmîm ... ʾet-hāʾĕlōhîm hithallek-nōaḥ; in Q he is warned not to be among the ignorant (innī aʿiẓuka an takūna mina l-jāhilīn) and pleads wa-illā taghfir lī wa-tarḥamnī akun mina l-khāsirīn.)
passages.text: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِى وَتَرْحَمْنِىٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

passages.note: What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts] (God's word about later generations is opposite: Gen promises no repeat (lōʾ-ʾōsip ʿôd lᵉhakkôt ʾet-kol-ḥay kaʾăšer ʿāśîtî), because the human heart is evil from youth; Q announces that some later nations will enjoy life and then be punished again (wa-umamun sa-numattiʿuhum thumma yamassuhum minnā ʿadhābun alīm).)
passages.text: וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת כָּל חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי

passages.note: What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts] (God's word about later generations is opposite: Gen promises no repeat (lōʾ-ʾōsip ʿôd lᵉhakkôt ʾet-kol-ḥay kaʾăšer ʿāśîtî), because the human heart is evil from youth; Q announces that some later nations will enjoy life and then be punished again (wa-umamun sa-numattiʿuhum thumma yamassuhum minnā ʿadhābun alīm).)
passages.text: قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

passages.note: Whether and how Noah speaks to God (Noah never speaks to God in Gen; he obeys and offers sacrifice (wayyiben nōaḥ mizbēaḥ laYHWH). In Q he calls to God for his drowned son (rabbi inna bnī min ahlī wa-inna waʿdaka l-ḥaqq), is rebuked, and asks for refuge and forgiveness.)
passages.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה

passages.note: Whether and how Noah speaks to God (Noah never speaks to God in Gen; he obeys and offers sacrifice (wayyiben nōaḥ mizbēaḥ laYHWH). In Q he calls to God for his drowned son (rabbi inna bnī min ahlī wa-inna waʿdaka l-ḥaqq), is rebuked, and asks for refuge and forgiveness.)
passages.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

passages.note: Whether and how Noah speaks to God (Noah never speaks to God in Gen; he obeys and offers sacrifice (wayyiben nōaḥ mizbēaḥ laYHWH). In Q he calls to God for his drowned son (rabbi inna bnī min ahlī wa-inna waʿdaka l-ḥaqq), is rebuked, and asks for refuge and forgiveness.)
passages.text: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبْنِى مِنْ أَهْلِى وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ

passages.note: Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits)
passages.text: וְהַמַּ֗יִם גָּֽבְר֛וּ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹ֖ד עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיְכֻסּ֗וּ כָּל הֶֽהָרִים֙ הַגְּבֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר תַּ֖חַת כָּל הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

passages.note: Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits)
passages.text: חֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה גָּבְר֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְכֻסּ֖וּ הֶהָרִֽים

passages.note: Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits) (No mountain gives refuge from the flood: saʾāwī ilā jabalin yaʿṣimunī mina l-māʾi qāla lā ʿāṣima l-yawma min amri llāh; fī mawjin ka-l-jibāl vs wayᵉkussû kol-hehārîm haggᵉbōhîm ... ḥămēš ʿeśrēh ʾammāh milmaʿlāh.)
passages.text: وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

passages.note: Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits) (No mountain gives refuge from the flood: saʾāwī ilā jabalin yaʿṣimunī mina l-māʾi qāla lā ʿāṣima l-yawma min amri llāh; fī mawjin ka-l-jibāl vs wayᵉkussû kol-hehārîm haggᵉbōhîm ... ḥămēš ʿeśrēh ʾammāh milmaʿlāh.)
passages.text: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِى مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ

passages.note: Why God destroyed a generation or a people (Why the generation drowns: in Q because they rejected the messenger (wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā); in Gen because the earth was full of violence and corruption (wattimmālēʾ hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô). Moral corruption becomes rejection of a prophet.)
passages.text: וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): contrast, divergence, echo, parallel. Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu). Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'. God tells Noah privately that the others will be destroyed by water: wa-ūḥiya ilā nūḥin annahu lan yuʾmina min qawmika illā man qad āmana ... innahum mughraqūn vs qēṣ kol-bāśār bāʾ lᵉpānay ... hinnî mēbîʾ ʾet-hammabbûl mayim. wa-ṣnaʿi l-fulka bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā vs ʿăśēh lᵉkā tēbat ʿăṣê-gōper. Gen gives the material, measurements and pitch (6:14-16); Q only 'under our eyes and our inspiration'. The sign that the flood begins: ḥattā idhā jāʾa amrunā wa-fāra t-tannūru (the oven boiled over) vs bayyôm hazzeh nibqᵉʿû kol-maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm rabbāh waʾărubbōt haššāmayim niptāḥû, dated to the 17th of the second month of Noah's 600th year. Q has a domestic oven instead of the cosmic deep and the windows of heaven, and no date. cf. b. Sanhedrin 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the canon. min kullin zawjayni thnayni vs šᵉnayim mikkōl ... zākār ûnᵉqēbāh. Q lacks Gen's second rule of seven pairs of clean animals (šibʿāh šibʿāh, Gen 7:2).

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Gen: Noah never speaks or prays; God chooses him as righteous (kî-ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq ləpānay) and tells him to enter with his household, and everything else is wiped out (wayyimaḥ ʾet-kol-hayqûm). Q: Noah calls out and is answered, idh nādā min qablu fa-stajabnā lahu fa-najjaynāhu wa-ahlahu ... fa-aghraqnāhum ajmaʿīn. Rescue by election becomes an answer to prayer, and the drowned are 'a people who denied our signs'.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); All others perish (weight 5.0); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 15.8.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 43 more.

Only in Noah answered; David and Solomon's judgment, the praising mountains, mail and wind: David and Solomon judge a case of sheep that strayed by night into a field; Solomon is given the right understanding; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail [contrast between the texts]; The people see that divine wisdom is in the king to do justice; The people see that divine wisdom is in the king to do justice [divergence between the texts]; Liability for one's grazing animals or spreading fire damaging another's field; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David [divergence between the texts]; God taught David the craft of making coats of mail; The stormy wind is subjected to Solomon, blowing at his command; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; Devils (shayāṭīn) and jinn labor for Solomon, diving and building; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents.

title: The Flood (full read) ↔ Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven
summary: These two units share 8 motifs: what the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts], when and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts], whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts], why god destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]….

passages.note: What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts] (End of the voyage: Genesis has the ark resting on the mountains of Ararat, an altar and burnt offerings whose odor God smells, then his promise never again to curse the ground (wa-yyiven Nōaḥ mizbēaḥ ... wa-yyāraḥ YHWH ʾet rêaḥ han-nîḥōaḥ ... lōʾ ʾōsif). The Quran has no altar, sacrifice or promise: Noah says al-ḥamdu lillāhi lladhī najjānā and prays rabbi anzilnī munzalan mubārakan, and the landing place is not named.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. an iṣnaʿi l-fulka bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā ~ ʿăśē ləkā tēvat ʿăṣê gōfer: God commands the vessel. Genesis gives the wood, pitch and dimensions (6:14-16), the Quran only says it is built 'under our eyes and our revelation'; the ark is fulk, not tēvâ. fa-sluk fīhā min kullin zawjayni thnayni ~ šənayim mi-kkōl tāvîʾ ʾel hat-tēvâ ... zākhār û-nəqēvâ: two of every kind. The Quran omits the sevens of clean animals (Gen 7:2), which prepare Noah's sacrifice. In Genesis Noah never speaks before the flood: wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ kə-khōl ʾăšer ṣiwwâ ʾōtô; he is chosen because God saw him righteous (ʾōtəkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq). In the Quran he is a messenger (arsalnā Nūḥan ilā qawmihi) who preaches 'yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu', and the chiefs answer that he is only a man like them, possessed (bihi jinna). Cause of the flood: Gen 6:13 kî mālʾâ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās, the earth filled with violence, and God's own decision (hinnî mašḥîtām); Q 23:26-27: they are drowned for rejecting the messenger (bimā kadhdhabūni ... alladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), and Noah asks for it (rabbi nṣurnī). Signal and source: Genesis gives a time (lə-yāmîm ʿôd šivʿâ ʾānōkhî mamṭîr) and waters from the burst springs of the deep and the windows of heaven (nivqəʿû kol maʿyənôt təhôm rabbâ wa-ʾărubbōt haš-šāmayim niftāḥû); the Quran gives a sign, 'when our command comes and the oven boils' (wa-fāra t-tannūr). cf. b. Sanh. 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the HB. Genesis saves the whole household, bōʾ ʾattâ wə-khol bêtəkā ... Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê vānāyw; the Quran excepts some: wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu minhum (the drowned son of 11:42-43), and forbids Noah to plead for the wrongdoers (wa-lā tukhāṭibnī fī lladhīna ẓalamū).

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Noah's role. Gen: Noah never speaks before the flood. He is ʾîš ṣaddîq tāmîm ... ʾet-hā-ʾĕlōhîm hithallekh-Nōaḥ, God speaks to him alone, and he obeys in silence. Q: Noah is a messenger who preaches, yā qawmi ʿbudū llāha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu, innī rasūlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna, ublighukum risālāti rabbī wa-anṣaḥu lakum. A silent righteous man becomes a warning prophet, the model of Muhammad. Why the flood comes. Gen: wat-timmālēʾ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô, universal violence and corruption. Q: fa-kadhdhabūhu fa-anjaynāhu ... wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā, the rejection of the messenger. The moral cause becomes a cause about revelation, and the drowned are 'a blind people' (qawman ʿamīna). Who is saved. Gen: bōʾ-ʾattāh wə-khol-bêtəkhā ʾel-hat-tēvāh; Nōaḥ û-vānāyw wə-ʾištô û-nəšê-vānāyw, his household. Q: fa-anjaynāhu wa-lladhīna maʿahu fī l-fulki, 'those with him', a community of believers rather than a family (cf. Q 11:46, where a son drowns).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.4); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 22.9.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 42 more.

Only in Noah warns his people: The drowned/destroyed were a blind people; People marvel that a reminder came through a man from among them; Prophet calls himself his people's sincere and trustworthy adviser (nasih amin); The righteous man's warning is taken as a joke by his own relatives; The chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him'; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Added role: in Genesis God speaks only to Noah (wa-yyōʾmer ʾĕlōhîm le-Nōaḥ qēṣ kol bāśār bāʾ le-fānay) and Noah never speaks to anyone; he only obeys (wa-yyaʿaś Nōaḥ ke-kōl ʾăšer ṣiwwāh ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm). In Q 71 Noah is a messenger and warner: yā-qawmi innī lakum nadhīrun mubīn, uʿbudū llāha wa-ttaqūhu wa-aṭīʿūn, preaching laylan wa-nahāran, jihāran, iʿlānan wa-isrāran. cf. 2 Pet 2:5, b. Sanh. 108 (Noah as preacher), not a match. Motive changed: Genesis gives moral corruption and violence (rabbāh rāʿat hā-ʾādām ... wa-ttimmālēʾ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās; hišḥît kol bāśār ʾet darkô). Q 71 gives rejection of the messenger and idolatry: rabbi innahum ʿaṣawnī ... wa-qālū lā tadharunna ālihatakum wa-lā tadharunna waddan wa-lā suwāʿan wa-lā yaghūtha wa-yaʿūqa wa-nasrā. Five named gods; Genesis names no god but YHWH/Elohim. Who calls for destruction is reversed: in Genesis God decides alone (wa-yyōʾmer YHWH ʾemḥeh ʾet hā-ʾādām; we-hinnî mašḥîtām ʾet hā-ʾāreṣ) and even regrets creating (wa-yyinnāḥem YHWH). In Q 71:26-27 Noah asks: rabbi lā tadhar ʿalā l-arḍi mina l-kāfirīna dayyāran, innaka in tadharhum yuḍillū ʿibādaka. There is no divine regret in the Quran. Rain reversed: in Genesis rain from opened sky is the destruction (wa-ʾărubbōt ha-ššāmayim niftāḥû, wa-yehî ha-ggešem ʿal hā-ʾāreṣ ʾarbāʿîm yôm). Noah in Q 71:10-11 promises rain as blessing if they repent: istaghfirū rabbakum ... yursili s-samāʾa ʿalaykum midrāran, then (71:25) mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū: the sky that could have blessed them drowns them. The saved are defined by faith, not by house: Gen 7:1 bōʾ ʾattāh we-kol bêtkā ʾel ha-ttēvāh kî ʾōtkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq. Q 71:28 rabbi ghfir lī wa-li-wālidayya wa-li-man dakhala baytiya muʾminan wa-li-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muʾmināt: whoever enters my house as a believer. Ending changed: Genesis ends with Noah's sacrifice and God's promise lōʾ ʾōsîf leqallēl ʿôd ʾet hā-ʾădāmāh ... we-lōʾ ʾōsîf ʿôd lehakkôt ʾet kol ḥay. Q 71 ends with the drowned sent on into fire (ughriqū fa-udkhilū nāran) and Noah's prayer of forgiveness and of destruction (wa-lā tazidi ẓ-ẓālimīna illā tabārā). No sacrifice, no covenant, no 'never again'.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Destruction motivated by human wickedness or violence [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Seek forgiveness and repent, and God will send the sky down on you in abundant rain [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.4); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.1); All others perish (weight 5.0). Pair score 48.1.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

Only in Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood: Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a fire; The people put their fingers in their ears and wrap their garments over their heads to avoid hearing the prophet; Noah's people refuse to abandon their gods Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; The flood hero prays for forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever enters his house believing, and all believers; God caused humans to grow from the earth like a plant, returns them to it and will bring them out again; Prophet summons his people night and day, openly and in secret, yet they only flee further; Human comes from dust and returns to dust [divergence between the texts]; God created seven heavens in layers (sab' samawat tibaqan) or built seven strong (heavens) above humans; The sun is made a lamp (siraj), a blazing lamp, and the moon a light (nur) within the heavens; God made the great lights: the sun to rule the day, the moon and stars to rule the night; Seek forgiveness and repent, and God will send the sky down on you in abundant rain; God spread out the earth as a carpet, cradle or bed (bisat, mihad, daha, sutihat, tahaha); and 6 more.

title: Sons of God, daughters of men, and the Nephilim ↔ Creation not in jest; the unceasing angels and the argument from one God
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: divine beings take human women as wives, those called god's offspring are rather honored servants who do not speak before him [response between the texts].

Genesis: zōʾṯ ʾôṯ hab-bərîṯ ... ʾeṯ qaštî nāṯattî be-ʿānān (the rainbow as covenant sign that it will not happen again). title: The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes ↔ Those who dispute about God and those who worship on an edge

passages.note: Worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit you (mā lā yanfaʿuhu ~ mâ-hôʿîl pesel 'what profit is an idol?': the uselessness (lack of benefit, hôʿîl / nafaʿa) of what is worshipped.)

passages.note: Worshipping what can neither harm nor benefit you (yadʿū min dūni llāhi mā lā yaḍurruhu wa-mā lā yanfaʿuhu ~ kî lōʾ yārēʿû wə-gam hêṭêv ʾên ʾôtām: the idol can do neither harm (raʿ / ḍarr) nor good (hêṭîv / nafʿ). passages.note: They will say to the mountains 'Cover us' and to the hills 'Fall on us' (law tusawwā bihimu l-arḍ; compare Hos 10:8)
passages.text: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَعَصَوُا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثًا

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Hos 10:8 wĕ-ʾāmĕrû le-hārîm kassûnû wĕ-la-gĕbāʿôt nipĕlû ʿālênû: they will say to the mountains 'cover us', to the hills 'fall on us'; Q 4:42 yawmaʾidhin yawaddu lladhīna kafarū ... law tusawwā bihimu l-arḍu: on that day the unbelievers will wish the earth were levelled over them. Wish to be buried under the land to escape judgment; Hosea's is the fall of Samaria's shrines, the Quran's the Last Day.

title: The throne vision and the call of Isaiah ↔ Believers, unbelievers and hypocrites
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: hardening of the heart, ears and eyes of the hearers [divergence between the texts], prophet commissioned to make the people's heart fat, ears heavy and eyes shut lest they understand and be healed.

Israel sees much but does not observe; The hypocrites try to deceive God, but it is he who deceives them; Hypocrites profess faith before believers and tell their own 'devils' in private they were only mocking; Who is called blind and deaf toward God's word [divergence between the texts]; and 4 more.

Only in Ahaz, the Syro-Ephraimite threat and the Immanuel sign: The child will eat curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil and choose good; 'If you do not believe (ta'aminu) you will not be established (te'amenu)': faith as condition of survival; God will whistle for the fly of Egypt and the bee of Assyria to settle in the land; God will shave head, 'hair of the feet' and beard with a razor hired beyond the River (the king of Assyria); King invited to ask any sign 'deep as Sheol or high as heaven' refuses, saying he will not test God; Cultivated land worth a thousand silver reverts to briers and thorns (shamir va-shayit), fit only for grazing and hunting; Enemy kings dismissed as two smoldering stumps of firebrands; Aram (Rezin) and Israel (Pekah) ally to attack Jerusalem and install a puppet king (son of Tabeel); A divine messenger announces a son to a virgin untouched by any man [divergence between the texts]; Before a child knows to refuse evil and choose good (or say 'father, mother') the enemy kings' lands will be deserted; Prophet meets the king at the conduit of the upper pool on the highway of the Fuller's Field; Prophet's child bears a symbolic name that is itself an oracle (Shear-yashuv, Maher-shalal-hash-baz); and 1 more.

Only in Healing of the city, the Righteous Branch and the covenant with day and night: God invites the prophet to call so he will reveal great and hidden things; God has a 'covenant with day and night' that fixes their order; David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of Israel; Flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them in the towns of Judah; God promises to bring healing and cure to the ruined city; The Levitical priests will never lack a man to offer sacrifice before God; People say God has rejected the two families he chose; The voice of the bridegroom and the bride will again be heard in the ruined land; Your Lord said 'Call on me and I will answer you'; God will cause a righteous Branch (tsemah) to sprout for David; The name 'YHWH is our righteousness' (YHWH tsidqenu); God's covenant with Israel is as sure as the fixed order of sun, moon, stars and sea; and 6 more.

Only in David's mountains, the two litigants and the ninety-nine ewes: Two litigants scale the wall of David's prayer-chamber (mihrab) and frighten him; A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's single ewe and overpowers him in argument; A case about a ewe is brought to David for judgment [divergence between the texts]; David realizes he was being tested, asks forgiveness, falls down bowing and turns in repentance; God strengthened David's kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive judgment (fasl al-khitab); David's repentance and what follows it [divergence between the texts]; A man with many sheep takes another's only ewe [divergence between the texts]; Shall God treat believers like those who spread corruption, the godfearing like the wicked?; The king confesses 'I have sinned' and the prophet announces forgiveness with a remaining penalty; A prophet tells a case as if real; the king condemns the offender and is told 'You are the man'; Mountains and birds are made to glorify God together with David; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth.

title: Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety ↔ Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release

Only in Oracle against Babylon (I): Bel and Merodach shamed, the hammer of the earth broken: Israel a scattered sheep: first Assyria devoured it, last Babylon gnawed its bones; Babylon's gods Bel and Merodach are put to shame and its idols dismayed; Desert creatures or demons (tsiyyim, iyyim) and ostriches inhabit the ruined city; God opens his armory and brings out the weapons of his indignation; Babylon called the 'hammer of the whole earth' is broken; Babylon is a land of idols, mad over their terrors; God's people are lost sheep whose shepherds led them astray on the mountains; Babylon addressed by wordplay names: Merathaim ('double rebellion') and Pekod ('punishment'); Repay the city according to her deeds: do to her as she has done; Israel's iniquity will be sought and not found, for God pardons the remnant; Repeated 'A sword upon...' litany against every class of a city; A day of vengeance belonging to YHWH of hosts against his foes; and 11 more.

title: Job - 'man born of woman'; the tree has hope ↔ Deniers demand their fathers; the people of Tubba'; the tree of Zaqqum; silk, brocade and the houris

Only in Covenant at Shechem; 'choose this day whom you will serve'; deaths of Joshua and Eleazar: God set darkness between Israel and the pursuing Egyptians; A priest is buried on the hill belonging to his son; Leader warns: you cannot serve YHWH, for he is a holy and jealous God; Joshua buried at Timnath-serah/heres north of Mount Gaash; The people are told to choose this day whom they will serve; The words of a covenant are written in a book of the law of God; Repeated mutual disavowal: 'I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship'; 'to you your religion and to me mine'; The people are made witnesses against themselves to their choice; God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the prophet under the tree (Bay'at al-Ridwan); Quraysh's security pact (ilaf) and caravan journeys of winter and summer; they should worship the Lord of this House who fed and secured them; A great stone set up as a witness because it has heard all God's words; God turned Balaam's curse into a blessing; and 9 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo, parallel. Abraham's father served other gods: teraḥ ʾăḇî ʾaḇrāhām ... wa-yaʿaḇḏû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm; wā-ʾeqqaḥ ʾeṯ ʾăḇîḵem ʾeṯ ʾaḇrāhām mē-ʿēḇer han-nāhār vs. wa-idh qāla ibrāhīmu li-abīhi wa-qawmihi innanī barāʾun mimmā taʿbudūn. Changed actor: in Joshua it is God who 'takes' Abraham away from his father's land and gods; in the Quran Abraham himself declares himself free (barāʾ) of his father's worship. Choosing the one God against the fathers' gods: wə-hāsîrû ʾeṯ ʾĕlōhîm ʾăšer ʿāḇəḏû ʾăḇôṯêḵem ... wə-ʾānōḵî û-ḇêṯî naʿăḇōḏ ʾeṯ YHWH vs. innanī barāʾun mimmā taʿbudūn illā lladhī faṭaranī fa-innahu sa-yahdīn. Joshua's 'I and my house' becomes Abraham's personal confession to his own father.
Shared motifs, rarest first: The people are told to choose this day whom they will serve (weight 6.7); Hero's father makes, sells or worships idols (weight 4.8). Pair score 11.5.

Only in Abraham disowns his father's worship; the great man of the two towns; silver roofs; the devil-companion: The damned wishes that between him and his companion lay 'the distance of the two easts'; But for fear all would become one community, God would give unbelievers houses with silver roofs, stairways, doors, couches and gold ornament; Abraham declares to his father and people that he is free of what they worship, except the one who created him; How Abraham parts from his father and his father's land or gods [divergence between the texts]; God expands provision (rizq) for whom he wills and restricts it; Lying on ivory beds eating lambs and calves, improvising on the harp like David, drinking wine from bowls and anointing with finest oils; What is given in this life is passing enjoyment (mata'); what is with God is better and more lasting; Opponents ask why the revelation was not sent down to some great man of the two towns; The wealth of the wicked: a scandal to be explained, or worthless enjoyment [divergence between the texts]; Abraham's confession is left as an enduring word among his descendants ('aqib); Whoever turns from God's remembrance is assigned a devil as constant companion (qarin), whom he curses at the judgment; The prophet cannot make the dead or deaf hear, nor guide the blind; and 2 more.

title: Covenant at Shechem; 'choose this day whom you will serve'; deaths of Joshua and Eleazar ↔ The pledge under the tree, the hidden believers in Mecca, the dream of entering the sanctuary, and the seed parable from Torah and Gospel
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: god was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the prophet under the tree (bay'at al-ridwan), sacred oak or terebinth marks a sanctuary site (moreh, mamre).

passages.note: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the prophet under the tree (Bay'at al-Ridwan) (A pledge of the people made under a sacred tree: wa-yiḵrōṯ yəhôšuaʿ bərîṯ lā-ʿām ... wa-yqîmehā šām taḥaṯ hā-ʾallâ ʾăšer bə-miqdaš YHWH vs. la-qad raḍiya llāhu ʿani l-muʾminīna idh yubāyiʿūnaka taḥta sh-shajara. title: Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan ↔ Badr and Uhud
summary: These two units share 3 motifs: a man secretly takes from the goods devoted to god (herem) [divergence between the texts], the army is defeated because of one member's hidden sin, a man secretly takes from the goods devoted to god (herem).

passages.note: A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) [divergence between the texts] (Josh 7:21 wā-ʾēreʾ ba-ššālāl ... wā-ʾeḥmĕdēm wā-ʾeqqāḥēm: Achan saw the spoil, coveted it and took it; 7:11 ḥāṭāʾ yiśrāʾēl ... lāqĕḥû min ha-ḥērem: the whole people is guilty; Q 3:152 wa-ʿaṣaytum min baʿdi mā arākum mā tuḥibbūn: you disobeyed after God showed you what you love (the spoils), and 3:161 wa-man yaghlul yaʾti bi-mā ghalla yawma l-qiyāma: whoever embezzles will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Josh 7:21 wā-ʾēreʾ ba-ššālāl ... wā-ʾeḥmĕdēm wā-ʾeqqāḥēm: Achan saw the spoil, coveted it and took it; 7:11 ḥāṭāʾ yiśrāʾēl ... lāqĕḥû min ha-ḥērem: the whole people is guilty; Q 3:152 wa-ʿaṣaytum min baʿdi mā arākum mā tuḥibbūn: you disobeyed after God showed you what you love (the spoils), and 3:161 wa-man yaghlul yaʾti bi-mā ghalla yawma l-qiyāma: whoever embezzles will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection. Lust for spoil causes defeat in both; Joshua's culprit is found by lot and executed with his family (7:24-25), the Quran defers the embezzler's punishment to the Last Day and states that no prophet would embezzle. Josh 7:7, 12 lāmâ heʿăbartā ... wĕ-lōʾ yukĕlû bĕnê yiśrāʾēl lāqûm lipnê ʾōyĕbêhem ... kî hāyû lĕ-ḥērem: Joshua asks God why they were defeated and is told it is the people's sin; Q 3:165 a-wa-lammā aṣābatkum muṣībatun ... qultum annā hādhā qul huwa min ʿindi anfusikum: when defeat struck you said 'how is this?'; say: 'it is from yourselves'. The question 'why?' after defeat, answered by the army's own guilt.

Shared motifs, rarest first: A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The army is defeated because of one member's hidden sin (weight 6.7); A man secretly takes from the goods devoted to God (herem) (weight 6.7). Pair score 20.1.

Only in Defeat at Ai and the trespass of Achan: The culprit is urged to 'give glory to God' by confessing; The sinner's children, animals and property are destroyed with him; Leader complains to God after a defeat: would that we had stayed where we were; Sin described as a sequence: I saw, I coveted, I took, I hid; Spies are sent ahead to scout a land for conquest; A great heap of stones is raised over an executed man, 'to this day'; Lot or Urim-Thummim cast to identify the guilty party (tamim); Leader and elders tear their clothes, fall on their faces and put dust on their heads; A place is named after an event that happened there, 'to this day'.

Only in Badr and Uhud: God helped you at Badr when you were weak; The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter; Such days God alternates among people; Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils); Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection; After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters; Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds; Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken; The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them; Those who restrain anger and pardon people; It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me; Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled; and 15 more.

title: The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty ↔ The hypocrites, deserters and those who offer peace
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: those allied by treaty or who withdraw and offer peace may not be attacked.

Same sequence: the young man destroys his father's people's cult objects unseen (wayyaʿaś lāylâ / baʿda an tuwallū mudbirīn), and the townsmen ask who did it, mî ʿāśâ haddābār hazzeh ... gidʿôn ben-yôʾāš ʿāśâ / man faʿala hādhā bi-ālihatinā ... samiʿnā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu Ibrāhīm. Gideon acts on God's command (wayyōʾmer lô YHWH); Abraham on his own oath (ta-llāhi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum). The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

A son destroys the cult objects of his father's house and the townsmen demand his death. Judg: wə-hārastā ʾeṯ-mizbaḥ ha-bbaʿal ʾăšer lə-ʾāḇîḵā ... hôṣēʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā wə-yāmōṯ; Joash answers ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreḇ lô (if Baal is a god let him fight for himself). Q: idh qāla li-abīhi wa-qawmihi mādhā taʿbudūn ... fa-rāgha ʿalayhim ḍarban bi-l-yamīn ... qālū bnū lahu bunyānan fa-alqūhu fī l-jaḥīm. In Judges the father defends the son by mocking the god; in the Quran the son mocks (mā lakum lā tanṭiqūn) and the father is the idolater.

Only in Al-Mujadila: the woman who disputed, the zihar formula and its expiation; God the fourth of three; the party of God: Before a private consultation with the prophet give charity (sadaqa); the rule is then relaxed; God has written: 'I will surely prevail, I and my messengers'; They greet the prophet with a greeting with which God did not greet him (al-sam for al-salam); When told to make room in assemblies, make room, and God will make room for you; rise when told to rise; The party of Satan (hizb al-shaytan) are the losers; the party of God (hizb Allah) are the successful; Secret counsels (najwa) for sin, aggression and disobedience are of Satan; confer rather in piety; God has heard the woman who argued with the prophet about her husband and complained to God (Khawla, 'she who disputes'); Expiation for zihar before touching again: free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor; There is no secret conversation of three but God is the fourth, nor of five but he is the sixth, wherever they are; God is well pleased with them and they with him (radiya llahu 'anhum wa-radu 'anhu); Expiation in steps according to what one can afford [divergence between the texts]; God will put his law within the people and write it on their hearts; and 9 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): echo. waylun li-kulli humazatin lumaza ~ lōʾ tēlēk rākîl be-ʿammêkā.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not go about as a talebearer among your people (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Be holy - ethical laws and love of neighbor: Do not stand idly by the blood of your neighbor; Do not take vengeance or bear a grudge against your people; Do not hate your brother in your heart; rebuke your neighbor instead; Each person must revere mother and father; Command 'You shall be holy, for I am holy'; A Quranic code of commandments resembling the Decalogue in content [divergence between the texts]; Fulfill God's covenant and do not break oaths after confirming them or use them for deceit; Love your neighbor as yourself; Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind; Sacrificial meat eaten on the third day is abhorrent (piggul) and the offering is invalid; The share of the poor in the owner's harvest or wealth [divergence between the texts]; If you retaliate, do so in kind; but patience is better; and 6 more.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand; Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.
